opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for his role. Full-time employees max out at write for systems they don't own, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E047 is a contractor with basic security training (note: HR lists full_time; security record shows contractor). As a contractor, max is read without advanced training, and admin is never permitted for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: HR (the authoritative source for employment type and role) lists E047 as a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write for systems not owned by their role. Requested admin exceeds the max of write, so grant write. (Note: Security's record lists contractor, which would max at read, but employment type is an HR fact and HR lists full_time; either way, requesting admin exceeds the maximum, and write is the max under the more authoritative HR record.)

- Security agent: role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up, same as HR), employment type: contractor (looked up in own database), security training: basic. Recommends read for Source Code.

So there's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. The employee is a Payroll Specialist, so does not own Source Code.
